# Theme Behaviour Checklist: Site foundation for doncoleman.ca

**Purpose**: Validate that the spec's and plan's requirements for dark/light theme behaviour are complete, unambiguous, consistent and measurable — covering the dark default, the three-state cycle, persistence, no-flash first paint, and reaction to system-preference changes.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) / [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements. It tests the requirements themselves, not the implementation.

## Dark Default Requirements

- [x] CHK001 Is "dark as the default" stated as unconditional for first-time visitors regardless of device preference, with no ambiguity about whether device preference should be consulted first? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, US2 Acceptance Scenario 1]
- [x] CHK002 Is the definition of "first-time visitor" (no stored choice) distinguished clearly from "stored choice unreadable/corrupted," which also falls back to dark, so the two paths aren't conflated in one requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011 vs. FR-015]
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec state whether the dark default applies identically to the not-found page and any future error states, or only to "any page" generically? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, FR-016]

## Three-State Cycle Requirements

- [x] CHK004 Is the cycle order (dark → light → match my device → dark) stated as the single authoritative sequence with no alternate ordering implied elsewhere in the spec? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, US2 Acceptance Scenario 2]
- [x] CHK005 Is the mechanism for triggering each transition (a single control, single activation gesture) specified precisely enough to prevent multiple interpretations (e.g., click vs. press-and-hold vs. separate buttons)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK006 Are the three states' visual/announced labels specified (what "match my device" is called to a visitor), so the announced text in US2 Acceptance Scenario 5 is verifiable? [Gap, Spec §US2 Acceptance Scenario 5]
- [x] CHK007 Is it specified whether the cycle position itself (not just the applied theme) must be preserved/restored across reloads, e.g., does re-entering "match my device" from a fresh load require the switch to already reflect that state? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012, FR-013]

## Persistence Requirements

- [x] CHK008 Is the persistence requirement explicit that no cookies are used, consistent between the theme requirements (FR-013) and the statistics requirements (SC-009), so there's no contradiction about storage mechanisms? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, SC-009]
- [x] CHK009 Is the storage key/location left fully to implementation, or does the spec/plan require a specific mechanism (e.g., `localStorage`) — and if the plan names one (`color-theme` in `localStorage`), is that reconciled with the spec's technology-agnostic wording? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013 vs. Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK010 Are the "missing, corrupted or unrecognised" stored-value cases each independently specified with the same fallback, or does only one case (missing) get explicit treatment while the others are inferred? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 Is behaviour specified for the case where storage can be read but not written (or vice versa), distinct from storage being entirely unavailable? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-015]
- [x] CHK012 Is "the site falls back to dark on the next load" (after a blocked-storage interaction) reconciled with "match my device" being an available in-session choice — i.e., is it clear the fallback applies only to the next *load*, not the current session? [Clarity, Spec §US2 Acceptance Scenario 6]

## No-Flash First Paint Requirements

- [x] CHK013 Is "no visible flash of the other theme" defined with an objective, testable threshold (e.g., zero frames of incorrect theme) rather than a subjective visual judgement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013, SC-003]
- [x] CHK014 Does the spec specify that the no-flash requirement holds across every entry point (direct load, in-site navigation, back/forward navigation), or only "reload... or open another page"? [Coverage, Spec §US2 Acceptance Scenario 3]
- [x] CHK015 Is the acceptance criterion in SC-003 ("first painted frame shows the correct theme every time") consistent with FR-013's "applied before the page is first painted," or could an implementation satisfy one without the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013 vs. SC-003]
- [x] CHK016 Is there a requirement addressing whether the no-flash guarantee must hold with JavaScript disabled, given the dark-only fallback in that case, or is that scenario explicitly out of the no-flash requirement's scope? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022, Edge Cases]

## System-Preference Change Requirements

- [x] CHK017 Is "follows it without a reload" specified with an expected responsiveness bound (immediate vs. eventually), or left fully open? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, US2 Acceptance Scenario 4]
- [x] CHK018 Is the scope of system-preference-change handling limited to when "match my device" is selected, and is it explicit that dark/light explicit choices do NOT react to system changes — avoiding a reader inferring otherwise? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014 vs. FR-011/FR-012]
- [x] CHK019 Is it specified what happens if the device preference changes while the tab is backgrounded/inactive — applied on next foregrounding, or only if the page is already visible? [Edge Case, Gap]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK020 Can "the site changes to light" / "returns to dark" (US2 Acceptance Scenario 2) be objectively verified without additional detail (e.g., which DOM/attribute signal indicates the active theme)? [Measurability, Spec §US2 Acceptance Scenario 2]
- [x] CHK021 Is SC-003's "repeated automated loads with each stored theme choice" specific enough about sample size or method to be a reproducible acceptance test, or is "repeated" left undefined? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK022 Is the assumption that browsers reliably expose a live-updating system colour-scheme media query (for FR-014) documented, including any fallback if a browser doesn't support live updates? [Assumption, Gap]
- [x] CHK023 Does the plan's choice of an inline `is:inline` pre-paint script versus a processed script get traced back to a spec requirement (FR-013's "before first paint"), confirming the two artifacts agree? [Traceability, Spec §FR-013 vs. Plan §First-party option table]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK024 Is there any conflict between "dark as the default" (FR-011) and "match my device" as a cycle option that a visitor could select and then have persisted as their default going forward — is the term "default" scoped correctly throughout? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, FR-012]
